title: Spring warmth gave no clear link to recorded late-window frog survey retention in four US samples in 2001-2015
abstract: We tested whether spring warmth predicts recorded late-window survey retention after an early frog survey. We used 3,921 route-years at 653 Northeast and Midwest US routes in 2001-2015. Four linear models controlled route and year effects. All four 95 percent temperature slope intervals included zero. Estimates ranged from -6.30 to +0.37 percentage points per C. The Northeast intervals were wide. Four sensitivity variants did not establish a repeated link. This is a test of retained public records, not animal abundance or volunteer motives. Selection on early reports, few year clusters, coarse weather and one monitoring system limit inference. The package gives code, annual evidence, source hashes, an independent numerical audit and a figure.

display.caption: Spring temperature slopes for recorded window-3 retention after a window-1 survey. All four primary intervals include zero.

citations.reason: We reuse verified temperature and eligible-run panels. We test annual window retention rather than calling-date shifts. Sources overlap.
